name: Detecting When Models Are Wrong or Biased
gist: Papers measure model uncertainty, robustness to tricky inputs, and hidden biases — catching cases where models confidently give wrong answers or fail on edge cases.
explain: A model can be confident and completely wrong. It might tell you a dog is a cat with 99% certainty. It might give different answers to the same question asked in different ways, even though any human would recognize they are the same. It might refuse to help a person with one name but help happily when the name changes, because it absorbed preferences from training data where one group was treated differently than another. This subtheme is about building tests that catch these failures: model uncertainty, inconsistency, what happens when you trick the model with small changes, and biases the model's creators never noticed.

Why is detecting wrongness hard? Because a model's internal confidence score (how sure it says it is) often has almost nothing to do with whether it is actually right. A model trained on biased data might genuinely believe something false. If you only test a model on clean, normal inputs, you might miss that it breaks on edge cases—unusual spellings, dialogs with strange background assumptions, images with weird lighting. And bias is sneaky: a model might behave identically on similar inputs except that one involves a person of a particular group, revealing invisible discrimination that no human explicitly programmed in. Researchers need tests that can catch these hidden problems before deployment to the real world.

Researchers build benchmarks to catch these problems in multiple ways. Some create stress tests: adversarial examples designed to fool the model, or tricky rewording of the same question to see if the model contradicts itself. Others gather data specifically about domains where bias is known to be a problem—hiring, criminal justice—and measure whether the model treats everyone fairly. Still others build datasets to test a model's calibration: is it right more often when it is confident, and wrong when it is uncertain? By running these tests before deployment, researchers can find and sometimes fix problems before the model is released into the world.

papers.title: AutoCode: LLMs as Problem Setters for Competitive Programming
papers.contribution: AutoCode test suites achieve 99% consistency with official judgments versus less than 81% for prior HardTests; produces novel problem variants and filters malformed problems, verified by Grandmaster-level (top 0.3%) competitive programmers to be of contest qua

papers.title: AutoMetrics: Approximate Human Judgments with Automatically Generated Evaluators
papers.contribution: Improves Kendall correlation with human ratings by up to 33.4% over LLM-as-a-Judge baseline while requiring fewer than 100 feedback points across diverse tasks.

papers.title: Dropping Just a Handful of Preferences Can Change Top Large Language Model Rankings
papers.contribution: Demonstrates rankings of top models can be remarkably sensitive; dropping just 0.003% of human preferences can change Chatbot Arena's top-ranked model.

papers.title: ExpGuard: LLM Content Moderation in Specialized Domains
papers.contribution: Deliver competitive performance on established benchmarks while demonstrating exceptional resilience to domain-specific adversarial attacks, surpassing WildGuard by up to 15.3%.

papers.title: Harnessing Temporal Databases for Systematic Evaluation of Factual Time-Sensitive Question-Answering in LLMs
papers.contribution: Enables scalable TSQA evaluation reducing human labor reliance while revealing how LLMs handle time references in explanations alongside answer accuracy.

papers.title: LLMs Get Lost In Multi-Turn Conversation
papers.contribution: All tested top LLMs show average 39% performance drop in multi-turn conversations; discovers that when LLMs take a wrong turn, they get lost and fail to recover.

papers.title: Local Success Does Not Compose: Benchmarking Large Language Models for Compositional Formal Verification
papers.contribution: Reveals 92% performance gap: while syntax correctness remains >99% for single-function tasks, it drops to 95.67% and verification crashes to 3.69% for compositional tasks.

papers.title: MolecularIQ: Characterizing Chemical Reasoning Capabilities Through Symbolic Verification on Molecular Graphs
papers.contribution: Enables fine-grained evaluation revealing that large MoE models lead while chemistry-tuned LLMs underperform generalist bases, indicating limited structural reasoning transfer.

papers.title: Non-Collaborative User Simulators for Tool Agents
papers.contribution: Reveals significant performance degradation in state-of-the-art tool agents under non-collaborative conditions, with detailed analysis of hallucinations and dialogue breakdowns.

papers.title: Semantic Visual Anomaly Detection and Reasoning in AI-Generated Images
papers.contribution: Models fine-tuned on AnomReason achieve consistent gains on semantic matching metrics, with applications to explainable deepfake detection and semantic reasonableness assessment.

papers.title: VPI-Bench: Visual Prompt Injection Attacks for Computer-Use Agents
papers.contribution: Current CUAs can be deceived at rates up to 51%, and browser-based agents at 100% on certain platforms; existing defenses offer only limited improvements.

papers.title: (Be Cautious!) Bio-Foundation Models Are Not Yet Robust to Biologically Plausible Perturbations and ML Transformations
papers.contribution: Reveals most bio-FMs are vulnerable to biological perturbations and ML transformations despite strong baseline performance, with cryo-EM models showing surprising robustness.

papers.title: A High Quality Dataset and Reliable Evaluation for Interleaved Image-Text Generation
papers.contribution: 25K-50K samples yield substantial improvements; scaling to 200K brings further gains in content and cross-modal synergy.

papers.title: A2ASecBench: A Protocol-Aware Security Benchmark for Agent-to-Agent Multi-Agent Systems
papers.contribution: The framework demonstrates that identified attacks are pervasive and highly effective, consistently bypassing default safeguards across travel, healthcare, and finance domains.

papers.title: Addressing Pitfalls in the Evaluation of Uncertainty Estimation Methods for Natural Language Generation
papers.contribution: Improves robustness of empirical assessment by marginalizing over multiple judge variants and exploring diverse evaluation settings.

papers.title: Analyzing and Evaluating Unbiased Language Model Watermark
papers.contribution: UWBench reveals that no unbiased watermark can perfectly preserve distribution under infinite queries and offers standardized benchmarking for advancing watermarking design.

papers.title: Are We Overconfident in Models and Results for Semi-Supervised 3D Medical Image Segmentation?
papers.contribution: Delivers strong performance under existing protocols; advocates for multiple-run reporting to establish more rigorous benchmarks with realistic perspective.

papers.title: Benchmarking at the Edge of Comprehension
papers.contribution: Demonstrates stable and externally correlating scores across eight frontier LLMs in mathematical domains without requiring full human comprehension of solutions.

papers.title: Beyond Classification Accuracy: Neural-MedBench and the Need for Deeper Reasoning Benchmarks
papers.contribution: Systematic evaluation reveals reasoning failures dominate model shortcomings compared to conventional datasets, establishing the necessity of depth-oriented compact benchmarks for reliable clinical reasoning assessment.

papers.title: BeyondBench: Benchmark-Free Evaluation of Reasoning in Language Models
papers.contribution: Evaluation of 101 language models shows consistent reasoning deficiencies, with performance degrading sharply as problem complexity increases from polynomial to exponential.

papers.title: Bongard-RWR+: Real-World Representations of Fine-Grained Concepts in Bongard Problems
papers.contribution: VLMs consistently struggle with discerning fine-grained concepts, highlighting limitations in abstract visual reasoning across diverse BP formulations.

papers.title: Cancer-Myth: Evaluating Large Language Models on Patient Questions with False Presuppositions
papers.contribution: No frontier LLM corrects false presuppositions more than 43% of the time, though GEPA raises accuracy to 80% at the cost of 41% misidentification on presupposition-free questions.

papers.title: Conditional Coverage Diagnostics for Conformal Prediction
papers.contribution: ERT provides conservative estimates of coverage miscoverage measures with higher statistical power than established metrics like CovGap, with an open-source implementation and benchmark across conformal methods.

papers.title: Conf-Gen: Conformal Uncertainty Quantification for Generative Models
papers.contribution: Enable formal guarantees on image generators producing non-memorized images, conversational AI asking enough clarifying questions, and agent output correctness.

papers.title: Conformal Calibration Transfer
papers.contribution: The method provides finite-sample target-domain coverage guarantees that adapt to observable mismatch magnitude without labeled target calibration.

papers.title: Conformal Reliability: A New Evaluation Metric for Conditional Generation
papers.contribution: Produces more informative prediction sets than existing approaches with verified coverage guarantees and demonstrated interpretability on image-to-text and text-to-image tasks.

papers.title: DEER: A Benchmark for Evaluating Deep Research Agents on Expert Report Generation
papers.contribution: Reveals current systems produce structurally plausible evidence-citing reports but struggle with expert-level satisfaction and logical completeness.

papers.title: EgoNight: Towards Egocentric Vision Understanding at Night with a Challenging Benchmark
papers.contribution: Constructs 3658 QA pairs across 90 videos spanning 12 VQA types with day-night alignment; reveals substantial performance drops from day to night, underscoring low-light reasoning challenges.

papers.title: Evaluating Robustness of Reasoning Models on Parameterized Logical Problems
papers.contribution: Reveals sharp performance transitions and brittleness regimes in LLM reasoners under targeted structural interventions even when surface statistics are held fixed.

papers.title: Expanding the AI Evaluation Toolbox with Statistical Models
papers.contribution: Shows how statistical modeling can improve uncertainty quantification and provides variance decomposition and item difficulty estimates across 22 frontier LLMs.

papers.title: FATE: A Formal Benchmark Series for Frontier Algebra of Multiple Difficulty Levels
papers.contribution: FATE-X is the first formal benchmark surpassing both PhD-level exam difficulty and Mathlib library coverage; best models achieve 3% on FATE-H and 0% on FATE-X, revealing a stark performance gap.

papers.title: Faults in Our Formal Benchmarking: Dataset Defects and Evaluation Failures in Lean Theorem Proving
papers.contribution: Proposes fault taxonomy, automated checkers, semantic audit prompts, and standards for formal math dataset creation; releases corrected snapshots.

papers.title: Formally Exploring Visual Anomaly Detection Evaluation Metrics
papers.contribution: Establishes SAAM-ALARM as a theoretically sound evaluation metric providing more nuanced performance assessment and stronger benchmarking standard.

papers.title: From Static Benchmarks to Dynamic Protocol: Agent-Centric Text Anomaly Detection for Evaluating LLM Reasoning
papers.contribution: The dynamic protocol systematically exposes corner-case reasoning errors in text anomaly detection that conventional benchmarks fail to reveal, enabling progressive LLM evaluation.

papers.title: GDGB: A Benchmark for Generative Dynamic Text-Attributed Graph Learning
papers.contribution: Enables rigorous evaluation of DyTAG generation through standardized benchmarks and an LLM-based multi-agent framework for reproducible benchmarking.

papers.title: GICDM: Mitigating Hubness for Reliable Distance-Based Generative Model Evaluation
papers.contribution: Restores reliable metric behavior and improves alignment with human assessment; resolves hubness-induced evaluation failures for generative models.

papers.title: Improving Backward Conformal Prediction via Non-Conformity Score Transformation
papers.contribution: Reduces average coverage gap from 4.20% to 1.12% on common benchmarks.

papers.title: JALMBench: Benchmarking Jailbreak Vulnerabilities in Audio Language Models
papers.contribution: Finds LALM safety strongly influenced by modality and architecture; text-based safety partially transfers to audio; interleaving audio-text enables cross-modal generalization.

papers.title: MC-Search: Evaluating and Enhancing Multimodal Agentic Search with Structured Long Reasoning Chains
papers.contribution: Benchmarks six leading MLLMs, reveals systematic issues in over/under-retrieval and modality-misaligned planning, and introduces Search-Align for process-supervised fine-tuning improving planning fidelity.

papers.title: MEnvAgent: Scalable Polyglot Environment Construction for Verifiable Software Engineering
papers.contribution: Improves Fail-to-Pass rates by 8.6% while reducing time costs by 43%, constructing MEnvData-SWE the largest polyglot verifiable Docker environments dataset with 1000 tasks across 10 languages.

papers.title: MLE-Smith: Scaling MLE Tasks with Automated Multi-agent Pipeline
papers.contribution: Generates 606 tasks spanning multiple categories from 224 real-world datasets; performance on generated tasks strongly correlates with human-designed task performance.

papers.title: MMBench-Live: A Continuously Evolving Benchmark for Multimodal Models
papers.contribution: Contains 5.9K newly generated instances with high answer correctness, updates cost ~$30 and take 1-2 hours, preserves stable model rankings and exhibits weaker memorization.

papers.title: MVI-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating Robustness to Misleading Visual Inputs in LVLMs
papers.contribution: Evaluates 18 state-of-the-art LVLMs, uncovering pronounced vulnerabilities and providing actionable insights for developing more robust models.

papers.title: MedLesionVQA: A Multimodal Benchmark Emulating Clinical Visual Diagnosis for Body Surface Health
papers.contribution: Exposes persistent gap with best MLLM at 56.2% versus primary physicians at 61.4% and specialists at 73.2%, underscoring need for trustworthy medical AI.

papers.title: Multimodal Fact-Level Attribution for Verifiable Reasoning
papers.contribution: Reveals even strong MLLMs hallucinate citations despite correct reasoning; trade-off between reasoning depth and verifiable attribution.

papers.title: Neural Theorem Proving for Verification Conditions: A Real-World Benchmark
papers.contribution: The benchmark evaluates LLMs on VC proving and reveals significant challenges remaining for practical program verification.

papers.title: Nonparametric LLM Evaluation from Preference Data
papers.contribution: Produces statistically efficient estimates, incorporates black-box ML and pre-trained LLM evaluators, suggests optimal preference data collection policies.

papers.title: OpenEstimate: Evaluating LLMs on Probabilistic Estimation with Real-World Data
papers.contribution: LM-elicited priors are worth approximately five samples from the underlying distribution; posteriors using LM priors tend to be more accurate than naive priors.

papers.title: Questioning the Coverage-Length Metric in Conformal Prediction: When Shorter Intervals Are Not Better
papers.contribution: Formally derives conditions under which interval length improvements are deceptive and provides empirical evidence across regression and classification tasks.

papers.title: R1-SyntheticVL: Is Synthetic Data from Generative Models Ready for Multimodal Large Language Model?
papers.contribution: R1-SyntheticVL trained on synthesized MMSynthetic-20K demonstrates superior performance on various benchmarks through adversarial synthesis.

papers.title: ReVSI: Rebuilding Visual Spatial Intelligence Evaluation for Accurate Assessment of VLM 3D Reasoning
papers.contribution: Enables more reliable and diagnostic assessment of spatial intelligence, revealing systematic VLM failure modes obscured by prior benchmarks.

papers.title: RouterArena: An Open Platform for Comprehensive Comparison of LLM Routers
papers.contribution: RouterArena introduces the first open platform for comprehensive LLM router comparison with initial leaderboard and detailed metrics comparison.

papers.title: RubricRobustness: Evaluating the Sensitivity of Rubrics-Based Benchmarks to Simple Perturbations
papers.contribution: Reveals systematic vulnerabilities in popular benchmarks and establishes perturbation-based sensitivity analysis as prerequisite for evaluation validity.

papers.title: SL-VC: A Benchmark and Automated Framework for Separation Logic Verification Condition Proving
papers.contribution: Demonstrates LLM-assisted proof synthesis for separation logic verification of real-world system software like LiteOS kernel and mini-gmp library.

papers.title: SWE-ABS: Adversarial Benchmark Strengthening Exposes Inflated Success Rates on Test-based Benchmark
papers.contribution: Strengthens 50.2% of instances (25.1× improvement) and rejects 19.78% of previously passing patches, dropping top agent score from 78.80% to 62.20% and reshuffling leaderboard.

papers.title: SpotIt: Evaluating Text-to-SQL Evaluation with Formal Verification
papers.contribution: Reveals that test-based methods overlook differences between generated and ground-truth queries, exposing gaps in current Text-to-SQL evaluation on the BIRD dataset.

papers.title: Stable Localized Conformal Prediction via Transduction
papers.contribution: Delivers more stable prediction sets than standard conformal methods, especially for localized approaches when calibration data are limited.

papers.title: TRAJECT-Bench:A Trajectory-Aware Benchmark for Evaluating Agentic Tool Use
papers.contribution: Reveals failure modes like tool confusion and parameter-blind selection, and identifies bottlenecks in scaling to mid-length trajectories.

papers.title: Take Note: Your Molecular Dataset Is Probably Aligned
papers.contribution: Documented and validated that QM9, QMugs, and OMol25 datasets contain systematic orientational bias that neural networks exploit, providing a cautionary insight for molecular machine learning practitioners.

papers.title: Teaching VLMs to Admit Uncertainty in OCR from Lossy Visual Inputs
papers.contribution: Maintained accuracy while achieving 0.685 F1 on uncertainty tags and introduced Blur-OCR benchmark for evaluating uncertainty-aware OCR.

papers.title: The Seismic Wavefield Common Task Framework
papers.contribution: Provides a structured foundation for rigorous head-to-head algorithm evaluation with hidden test sets, revealing strengths and limitations of methods for reconstructing seismic wavefields from sparse measurements.

papers.title: TokSuite: Measuring the Impact of Tokenizer Choice on Language Model Behavior
papers.contribution: Enables robust decoupling of tokenizer influence with findings elucidating benefits and shortcomings of popular tokenizers across languages.

papers.title: ULTRA-360: Unconstrained Dataset for Large-scale Temporal 3D Reconstruction across Altitudes and Omnidirectional Views
papers.contribution: Benchmarks calibration and reconstruction algorithms, identifying areas for improvement in feature matching, densification, and multi-appearance handling.

papers.title: UniCode: Augmenting Evaluation for Code Reasoning
papers.contribution: Reveals 31.2% performance collapse in state-of-the-art models and identifies seed-problem regression patterns showing fragility under structural shifts.

papers.title: VocSim A Training-free Benchmark for Zero-shot Content Identity in Single-source Audio
papers.contribution: Frozen Whisper features with simple pooling and PCA achieve strong zero-shot performance with stable rankings across domains, revealing a cross-lingual speech generalization gap on low-resource languages.

papers.title: WinDeskGround: A Benchmark for Robust GUI Grounding in Complex Multi-Window Desktop Environments
papers.contribution: Evaluates five leading MLLMs on 1,356 instruction-target pairs, showing accuracy declines under partial occlusion.
